description:
Measured 2026-09-15: fz2 run fixtures2/behavior/json_roundtrip.fz takes 3.5s; with --log-telemetry it takes 50-62s for 40,743 records (23.7 MB), while enum_take_drop_split with 45,600 records goes 4.6s to 5.1s. A sample of the instrumented run puts 98.3% of samples in TyCanon::render -> descr_body -> axes -> clause_texts::<ArrowSig> -> func_clause -> conj_text, entered from JsonlBackend::append_self_describing -> CanonStream::define (src/telemetry/jsonl.rs ~199). define dedupes defined types at the top, but the render has no memo inside its recursion: one sampled render expanded into 118,041 clause_texts frames. JSON decoders are deeply nested arrows, and rendering is combinatorial in that depth.

Consequence: the project's prescribed diagnostic (minimal job-trace acceptance, .agent/docs/performance-instrumentation.md) cannot be run on the goal program, and every telemetry-derived timing on it is inflated 13-16x. Canon strings are display-only by rule, so this cost must not exist.

Fix: memoize the render per interned Ty (or per denotation once fz-kdt.48 lands) so each sub-type renders once per stream; a deterministic pin is the count of clause_texts calls per stream for json_roundtrip. Signal: the instrumented run within 1.5x of the plain run on json_roundtrip.

comments.text: 2026-09-16 re-check at 969caf165: current local release reproduction does not meet the old magnitude. `fz2 run fixtures2/behavior/json_roundtrip.fz` was 0.326 s; `fz2 --log-telemetry <path> run ...` was 0.409 s (1.25x) for 45,974 records, already within the ticket’s 1.5x signal. Do not implement against the 14x sample without reproducing it on the slow runner. Source review corrects one detail: TyCanon already memoizes whole/body/fingerprint per instance, but CanonStream::define constructs a fresh instance per definition batch, so cross-batch sharing is still absent. If the slow-runner issue recurs, measure clause render calls and use a stream-owned direct Ty-indexed table rather than another structural hash cache.

title: TyCanon::render is combinatorial in nested-arrow depth, so --log-telemetry costs 14x the compile on the goal program
